stem: Taylor has social anxiety. Taylor often ruminates how people will shun her and speak negatively behind her back. Which of the following categorization is most appropriate for this symptom?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Taylor is catastrophizing in this example and is best marked as a cognitive symptom. If, for example, Taylor was feeling sad or anxious this would be categorized as emotional. If, for example, Taylor began sweating and was tense this would be a physical symptom. If Taylor avoided social interactions this is a behavioral symptom.

stem: Which of the following would allow a physician to diagnose an anxiety disorder?

options.html: A patient scores 27 (the highest possible score) on the PHQ9 assessment
A patient scores 4/4 on the CAGE questions
For twelve months, about one week per month, a patient reports symptoms indicative of anxiety that occasionally interfere with functioning.
A patient has had six months of sustained symptoms of anxiety that interfere with functioning.
A patient has had three days of crippling symptoms of anxiety to the point where he has not left home.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

According to the DSM-5, to be diagnosed with an anxiety disorder, symptoms must be sustained for 6 months and they must have a significant interference with normal functioning.

stem: On Superbowl Sunday, Dr. Rivera hosts all the 2024’s over for a party to teach about hormonal regulation of hyperosmolarity. She supplies endless chips and nachos but her plumbing is broken so she cannot offer water. Which statement is true?

options.html: Prolonged hyperosmolarity can lead to fatal brain swelling.
Prolonged hyperosmolarity can lead to fatal brain swelling.
Less aldosterone will be secreted by the adrenal cortex.
There will be a dramatically increased secretion of renin from the kidneys.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Aldosterone signals kidneys to reabsorb water indirectly, by directly reabsorbing sodium. Due to hyperosmolarity of blood, to prevent further hyperosmolarity, the kidneys will reabsorb less sodium.

stem: A baby is born with renal tubular dysgenesis (you do not need to know what this condition is to answer this question). This is an autosomal recessive condition which can be caused by loss-of-function mutations in the gene that encodes angiotensin- converting-enzyme. This enzyme converts angiotensin I into angiotensin II. What clinical manifestations are expected as a result of this mutation?

options.html: The baby should have very low blood pressure.
The baby should have a large blood volume.
The baby might suffer from chronic hypernatremia.
The baby will have chronic hypertension.
There will be excessive aldosterone in the bloodstream.

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Angiotensin II is an intermediary in the RAAS pathway, which increases blood pressure by vasoconstriction, signals the release of vasopressin from the hypothalamus, and signals the release of aldosterone from the adrenal cortex. Aldosterone then signals the kidneys to reuptake sodium and water from urine. In the absence of angiotensin II, low blood volume and low blood pressure will result.

stem: Taylor is stranded in the desert and is in urgent need of a water source. Her blood pressure has become notoriously low and she is at risk of shock. Which of the following are increased as DIRECT result of high blood osmolarity?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Vasopressin is activated when osmolality is high or when there is low blood volume, which leads to increased permeability in the kidney and water being retained in the blood to preserve blood volume. Angiotensin II and Aldosterone are part of the RAAS pathway that is initiated when the kidney detects low blood pressure. Angiotensin II leads to vasoconstriction, and aldosterone leads to the kidney reabsorbing sodium and water from urine). Atrial Natriuretic Peptide is secreted from the atria of the heart when the blood pressure is too high as monitored by stretch receptors. This consequently leads to sodium and water leaving the body (through the kidneys), reducing the blood pressure.

weekLabel: Week 5 - Body Fluids, Blood Pressure & Screening

stem: The autonomic nervous system is associated with the regulation of blood pressure. Which statement below is true?

options.html: When the parasympathetic nervous system receives signals from baroreceptors in the aorta and carotid arteries it will result in vasoconstriction.
The sympathetic nervous system increases stroke volume and decreases heart rate.
The tonic activity of the sympathetic nervous system increases as a result of increased blood pressure
The parasympathetic nervous system decreases blood pressure by increasing the stroke volume.
The constriction and dilation of blood vessels is controlled exclusively by the sympathetic nervous system.

answer:
The correct answer is E.

Innervation of blood vessels by the sympathetic nervous system causes constriction. The parasympathetic nervous system does not directly cause vasodilation, but activation of the PNS shuts down the SNS, allowing for reduced vasoconstriction, or vasodilation.

weekLabel: Week 5 - Body Fluids, Blood Pressure & Screening

stem: Complete the sentence: When it comes to hormonal regulation of blood pressure,

options.html: Aldosterone increases the reabsorption of potassium in the kidneys.
Vasopressin in high amounts can act as a vasodilator.
Epinephrine can both dilate and constrict blood vessels, depending on the location of the epinephrine receptors.
Renin is secreted by the kidneys when there is high blood pressure.
Dehydration results in secretion of atrial natriuretic factor from the atrial regions of the heart.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Epinephrine binds to alpha-receptors and causes vasoconstriction, but also binds to betareceptors in the blood vessels of skeletal and cardiac muscle, causing vasodilation.

answer:
The correct answer is B.

The arterioles experience the largest drop in blood in blood pressure and are appropriately termed resistance vessels.

stem: Which of the following are plausible mechanisms that will decrease mean arterial blood pressure?

options.html: Up-regulating Sympathetic innervation to the heart
Down-regulating Parasympathetic innervation to the heart
Down-regulating Sympathetic innervation to the arterioles
Up-regulating Parasympathetic innervation to the arterioles

answer:
The correct answer is C.

By decreasing sympathetic innervation to the arterioles, blood vessels can dilate, thereby reducing total peripheral resistance and decreasing mean arterial blood pressure. Arterioles do not have parasympathetic innervation. Increasing sympathetic innervation to the heart or decreasing parasympathetic innervation to the heart will both lead to an increase in the heart rate, increasing cardiac output and thereby increasing mean arterial pressure.

The correct answer is D.

The Celcus tetrad is rubor (redness), calor (heat), dolor (pain), and tumor (swelling). Loss of function (not motility) was added as a fifth indication in the 19th century.

stem: Complete the following sentence: When tissue is damaged, the final result can be ____.

options.html: Regeneration, which involves secretion of growth factors that inhibit cell replication
Regeneration, if there are stem cells present to replace the tissue
Regeneration, if the damaged tissue is phagocytized quickly enough
Fibrous scar formation, if the tissue was only slightly damaged
Fibrous scar formation, if the tissue was made of cells that can proliferate

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Regeneration involves cells that can undergo mitosis when tissue damage is less severe. Reparation occurs in tissue with cells that cannot replicate, or when tissue damage is severe, resulting in scarring.

stem: Taylor gains a significant amount of weight. One complication is increased lipid storage in individual adipocytes. Which of the following adaptive responses describes the necessary change in her adipocytes?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Hypertrophy is an increase in cell size. Lipid deposition into her adipocytes will lead to an increase in cell size. With increased fat intake her adipose tissue will also increase its ability to store fat by undergoing hyperplasia.

stem: Which of the following does NOT correctly describe a stage of the inflammatory response?

options.html: Recognition: An offending agent is recognized by host cells and molecules
Recruitment: Leukocytes and plasma proteins are recruited from circulation
Regulation: The leukocyte and proteins are activated and eliminate the offending agent
Resolution: The damaged tissue is repaired

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Regulation involves controlling and terminating the inflammatory response. The definition given in this answer best applies to the “removal” stage of the inflammatory response.

stem: Taylor recently suffered a severe myocardial infarction and has been recovering at home for the past 6 months. Which of the following would you expect when examining her heart?

options.html: Her heart would have scar tissue deposition and would likely function as it had prior to the MI
Her heart would have scar tissue deposition and would have diminished myocardial function in the region of the MI
Her heart would undergo regeneration and would likely function as it had prior to the MI
Her heart would undergo regeneration and would have diminished myocardial function in the region of the MI

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Cardiac myocytes have very limited regenerative capacity; thus scar tissue is deposited at the site of major injury and this often leads to less-than-optimal functioning.

weekLabel: Week 5 - Body Fluids, Blood Pressure & Screening

stem: Taylor recently suffered a severe myocardial infarction and has been recovering at home for the past 6 months. Which of the following would you expect in Taylor’s remaining cardiac myocytes after an extended period of time?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Remaining cardiac myocytes have very limited regenerative capacity, thus hyperplasia is not a viable repair mechanism following myocardial infarction. Cardiac myocytes may experience hypertrophy to compensate for the loss in function in the infarcted area.

options.html: Veins carry blood toward the heart
There are three layers to both veins and arteries
Arterioles and venules connect via capillaries
More blood volume exists in arteries than in veins

answer:
The correct answer is D.

While D is true most of the time, by definition, arteries carry blood away from the heart. Pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood to the lungs.

stem: Key Feature Question: In which organs are wastes broken down or removed from the blood? (the number of correct answers is intentionally not given, should be given on a test)
answer:
The correct answer is B, C, F, G, I.

All of these organs have a role in removal of wastes: Lungs remove CO2; Lymph nodes digest pathogens; The liver processes waste metabolites; the spleen removes aged red blood cells; the kidneys remove wastes from the blood.

stem:
There are several different systems in the human body and all need to be supplied with blood. Which statements below are true? i) Endocrine signaling involves secreting hormones into the bloodstream and therefore is a slower signaling pathway than other direct methods.

  1. More red blood cells enter splenic arteries compared to splenic veins.
  2. Half of lymph returns to the cardiovascular system through the right lymphatic duct
answer:
The correct answer is D.

When hormones are secreted into the bloodstream, they return to the heart through veins, then to and from the lungs, and then from the heart to its target organs. This indirect signaling is slower than other direct methods such as nerve impulse propagation, for example. Spleens are the site of red-blood cell digestion, after about 120 days of activity. The Right Lymphatic duct brings lymph from half of the head, and the right side of the thoracic and abdominal cavities. However, lymph from the lower extremities and pelvic cavities re-enters circulation only via the thoracic duct.

stem: The autonomic nervous system is subdivided into two divisions: the sympathetic nervous system and the parasympathetic nervous system. Which statement below is true?

options.html: The sympathetic nervous system branches from the spinal cord using cranial and thoracic nerves.
The parasympathetic nervous system innervates the gut to halt digestion.
At least some portion of all pre-synaptic nerve fibres in the sympathetic nervous system are localized inside the sympathetic chain.
Parasympathetic nerves have a short pre-synaptic fiber and a long post-synaptic fiber.
Referred pain above the pelvic pain line reaches the central nervous system through the parasympathetic nerve pathways.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

All four nerve pathways in the sympathetic nervous system involve a pre-synaptic nerve fiber in the synaptic chain. In pathways 1,2 and 3, the synapses occur in the sympathetic chain. In pathway 4, the pre-synaptic nerve fiber passes through the sympathetic chain, synapsing in the paravertebral ganglia.

stem: Which option correctly describes a component of the nervous system?

options.html: The dorsal rami are associated with the skin and deep muscles of the back.
The ventral root contains afferent and efferent nerves.
Interneurons are a part of the reflex arc and allow for quick conduction of nerve impulses to the brain and back.
The Vagus nerve is a major nerve of the sympathetic nervous system.
In times of distress, salivation is halted by sympathetic nerves leaving the spinal cord through cranial nerve pairs

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Dorsal rami innervate the skin and deep muscles of the back. Ventral roots contain only efferent nerves. Interneurons do not involve brain processing but by-pass the brain. The Vagus nerve is associated with the parasympathetic nervous system. Sympathetic nerves are thoracolumbar, not cranial.

options.html: A pre-ganglionic nerve originates from the Intermediolateral horn of the spinal cord at the T1 level and then synapses with the post ganglionic neuron in the sympathetic trunk at the cervical ganglia.
A pre-ganglionic nerve originates from the Intermediolateral horn of the spinal cord at the T1 level and then synapses with the post ganglionic neuron in the sympathetic trunk at the same level
A pre-ganglionic nerve originates from the Intermediolateral horn of the spinal cord at the C1 level and then synapses with the post ganglionic neuron in the sympathetic trunk at the same level
A pre-ganglionic nerve originates from the Intermediolateral horn of the spinal cord at the C1 level and then synapses with the post ganglionic neuron in the sympathetic trunk at the cervical ganglia

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Sympathetic innervation from the intermediolateral horn only occurs in the T1-L3 region of the spinal cord and to innervate higher or lower structures, the preganglionic neuron synapses with the post ganglion neuron at a different level in the sympathetic chain.

stem: Taylor is experiencing severe diffuse pain on the surface of her upper leg and groin area (innervated by spinal nerves from S2-S4). After a physical exam, the doctor ruled out somatic leg pain. Which of the following internal structures should the doctor consider in this scenario?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

The pelvic pain line corresponds to the lower limit of the peritoneum. Structures directly above it (uterus in women and the superior surface of the bladder in men) are innervated by the TLL-12 region, while structures below (cervix and male genitals) are innervated by S2- 4.

stem: An amateur analyst looks at the preliminary data of a new screening program and notices that patients who are screened have longer survival (defined as the time from disease detection to death) than those who did not undergo screening. He concludes the screening program is effective and should be instituted. Which of the following biases is most applicable to this situation?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Lead-time bias refers to a phenomenon where early detection of a disease in an asymptomatic patient falsely appears to extend the length of survival, in comparison to a patient whose disease is detected only after symptoms develop.

stem: Taylor recently had a biopsy of a tumour on her right breast – the pathologist reports a highgrade carcinoma. What does this mean?

options.html: The tumour cells are confined by the basement membrane
The tumour cells will spread to lymph nodes
The tumour cells are highly abnormal relative to their tissue of origin
The tumour has a well-organized architecture

answer:
The correct answer is C.

The grading of a neoplasm refers to how well it histologically (microscopically) resembles the normal tissue from which it originates. High grade carcinomas usually show loss of the normal architectural patterns and also abnormal looking cells – this cellular change is called “pleomorphism”. Invasive carcinoma means a tumour has broken through the basement membrane. Although many high grade tumours will spread to lymph nodes or other parts of the body, this cannot be inferred from the statement in the question stem.

stem: A physician receives a pathology report indicating that her patient has a tumor with staging T2N1MX. Which statement below is true?

options.html: The tumour is almost certainly high grade as low grade tumours do not spread to lymph nodes
The cancer has spread to non-regional lymph nodes
The tumour shows a positive resection margin
Based on the findings of the pathological report, we do not know if metastasis has occurred
The tumour has shown distant spread and cure is not possible

answer:
The correct answer is D.

The “X” after the M in the TM staging system means that metastasis is unknown based on this pathologic resection. In this system, T refers to the tumour, usually its size or depth of invasion depending on the organ involved, N refers to the lymph-node status, and M refers to metastasis. In most organ systems, non-regional (distant) lymph nodes affect the M category.

options.html: A breast cyst is usually filled with fluid or air
Fibrocystic change is indicative of a neoplasm
A fibroadenoma is a neoplasm of the breast

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Fibrocystic change may be a result of cysts and/or fibrous tissue development leading to lumpy breasts, but it is not a tumour or neoplasm.

stem: Wendy, a 47-year old mother of two teens comes to your practice concerned about a lump in her breast. Her dad was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer at age 75 and passed away shortly thereafter. What one of the following would you tell your patient?

options.html: Tell the patient that we should immediately start aggressive treatment options.
Reassure the patient that lumps in the breast do not always indicate cancer, and further testing is needed
Advise the patient that her father’s pancreatic cancer may have metastasized to her during fertilization.
nform her that the tumour present is a high-grade carcinoma which can be treated hormonally.
Write a doctor’s note to excuse her from work and tell her to rest for a few days.

answer:
The correct answer is B.

A breast lump may mean a malignant tumour, but it may also be a fibroadenoma, cyst, fibrocystic change, or abscess, all of which are benign. Further testing should be done to confirm a diagnosis. A and C.

stem: The pathology report on your patient Alicia indicates a benign breast tumour (fibroadenoma). Which of the following describes the characteristics of this tumour? Select all that apply.
answer:
The correct answer is A, C, E.

Benign breast tumours tend to be firm, mobile, and sometimes tender with the menstrual period. Conversely, breast cancers tend to be hard, immobile, irregular, fixed to tissue and consistently painless. A. FNAP is usually used for lymph nodes.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

High risk patients are screened with MRI. Remember to use choosing wisely concepts. A PET scan is not the best choice resource-wise. C. Dysplasia is the presence of abnormal cells

stem: A medical oncologist wants to know if a patient’s breast cancer has metastasized to their axillary lymph nodes. Which of the following biopsy type should the oncologist choose?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

FNA is the most minimally invasive procedure and can be used primarily for palpable superficial lesions in the breast, thyroid, lymph node, salivary glands. A punch biopsy is not appropriate, as this is not a skin lesion. Incisional & excisional biopsies are not the first investigations of choice since they are more invasive and require more equipment, sterile conditions and more time.

stem: Your patient Kathleen has a palpable mass in her left breast which is irregular with an associated skin lesion. She is concerned about breast cancer due to a family history of breast cancer. Which of the following investigation is not appropriate in this scenario?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Currently there is no blood test to detect breast cancer. This could be a topic for your Experiential Learning research! The other modalities could be used to obtain a diagnosis, with the best choices B & C. FNA cannot identify invasion, however if clinically there is skin involvement (invasion) from the underlying breast cancer, then it is not necessary to see invasion and an FNA may be appropriate here.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which one of the following definitions is incorrect?

options.html: A high grade tumour is fast-growing
Neoadjuvant chemotherapy is given before surgical resection.
Dysplasia refers to a neoplasm that has spread to lymph nodes
Leukemia is a cancer of the bone marrow and blood
Hematogenous spread is a type of cancer spread

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Dysplasia refers to a group of cells showing an abnormal pattern of growth and maturation which is confined to the epithelium without breaking through the basement membrane, so there is no invasion into underlying tissues. Dysplasia cannot spread to lymph nodes since it has not gained access to the underlying tissues yet.

stem: Which one of the following is correct regarding The Two-Hit Theory of Cancer?

options.html: Cancerous cells must have 2 or more mutations in their genome
Receiving damage to 2 genes on the same chromosomes can produce cancer
Having damage to the same gene on both chromosomes can produce cancer
Receiving damage to the same gene 2 times can produce cancer

answer:
The correct answer is C.

If a cell receives damage to the same gene on both chromosomes this can produce cancer. The first hit can be inherited and second hit can be attained through life. C. FIT tests are usually done for CRC screening. Colonoscopy only for high-risk individuals.

stem: Gene A (which codes for your eye colour) becomes mutated and leads to your eye cells becoming cancerous. Which one of the following describes Gene A prior to becoming mutated?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

A proto-oncogene is a normal gene which when altered by a mutation becomes an oncogene. An oncogene is a mutated gene that can transform a normal cell into a cancer cell. A tumour suppressor gene is a gene that normally inhibits the cell cycle. B. The rest are all modifiable risk factors.

stem: Avery is a 35-year old female who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. Avery received radiation prior to surgery and post-surgery chemotherapy. Which of the following statements regarding the role of each treatment is correct?

options.html: Radiation is neoadjuvant, chemotherapy is adjuvant.
Radiation is adjuvant, chemotherapy is post-adjuvant.
Radiation is adjuvant, chemotherapy is neoadjuvant.
Radiation is palliative, chemotherapy is adjuvant.

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Neoadjuvant therapy is given prior to surgery and aims to reduce the size of the tumour, adjuvant therapy is given after surgery and aims to treat micro-metastatic disease.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical characteristic of a screening test?

options.html: Screening tests are cheap and easy
Screening tests are for the asymptomatic population
Screening tests are done for rare problems

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Screening tests are usually done for common problems.

From 07 - Well Person Care and Screening for Cancer. The lecture defines screening in one sentence: we screen for relatively common problems in people who are asymptomatic, using cheap and easy tests, for conditions where early detection allows effective but less invasive treatment. A rare problem breaks that model - a test run on a low-prevalence population yields few true cases for the cost and many false positives.

  • A - cheap and easy: a stated feature.
  • B - asymptomatic population: a stated feature.
  • C - less invasive: stated, both of the test and of the treatment early detection allows.

stem: BRCA-1 and BRCA-2 are tumour-suppressor genes. Only one functional copy of the gene is required to prevent cancer. Despite this, heterozygous carriers of a mutation in BRCA- 1 or BRCA-2 often develop cancer. Why is this?

options.html: Genetic mosaicism predisposes individuals to either ovarian cancer or breast cancer, regardless of the recessive nature of these genes.
Mutations to BRCA-1 or BRCA-2 produce variants of unknown significance; It is difficult to predict if a mutation will lead to cancer or not.
A deleterious mutation to the BRCA-1 or BRCA-2 genes in homozygotes leaves an additional copy of functional BRCA-1 or BRCA-2. Heterozygotes do not have this advantage.
Since most breast cancers are non-hereditary, BRCA-1 and BRCA-2 is not the best predictor whether a patient will develop breast cancer or not.

Due to their presence on the X-chromosome, females are more at risk of cancer arising from BRCA-1 or BRCA-2 mutations because of X-inactivation during embryonic development, and males are more at risk because they only have one X- chromosome.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

This question refers to the two-hit hypothesis. Homozygotes have an extra buffer of protection with two functional gene copies. However, with carriers of a BRCA-1 or BRCA- 2 mutation, if the single functional copy of BRCA-1/2 mutates, cancer may result (assuming other genes mutate as well)

Centenarians tend to score high on neuroticism and high on extraversion

Genetics are only a small component of a long life.

The correct answer is D.

By definition, age-related changes are universal in a species. Option A is a description of life expectancy, but lifespan, the highest age reported by a species has remained unchanged since 1997. Centenarians tend to score low on neuroticism. Since elder patients have a decreased antibody response, it is more important for them to take a yearly flu shot if possible. Lastly, genetics plays a large role in living a long life.

THE FOLLOWING QUESTION STEM APPLIES TO THE NEXT TWO QUESTIONS!

You are a physician seeing a new patient, Alice. Alice is 84 years old and states that she feels

well today. Her husband passed away three years ago. She drove to the clinic today and you

noticed a sizeable dent in her car when entering the clinic. She claims that she was side-swiped

in city traffic last month. She scored [24+1] on the MoCA when completed today, losing most of

her points in the serial sevens. Her vision and hearing were recently tested and no abnormalities

were identified.

She complains of fatigue at times and the occasional headrush when standing up quickly. Past-

medical history includes three instances of post-partum depression (PPD) and has been pregnant

six times. Current medication includes over-the-counter calcium supplements (500mg) and

physician-prescribed antipsychotic sleeping pills (Seroquel, an antipsychotic), without which she

cannot fall asleep. When you question her about her ADLs and IADLs, she is mostly

independent but requires help with finances from her adult son ever since the passing of her

husband, who primarily took care of finances. She seems peppy during your interview and she

relates that her greatest pleasure is spending time with her great- grandchildren, who are 3 and 7.

She watches them during the week while her grandchildren work full- time jobs.

stem: What first intervention might you suggest to help manage this patient’s fatigue?

options.html: Ask her to complete a driving assessment
Inquire about the use of her antipsychotic medication and attempt to reduce the dose
Given her MoCA, diagnose her with dementia and begin interventions to target this
Examine her for orthostatic hypotension and treat this with medications

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Antipsychotic drugs in the elderly are associated with fatigue, weight gain, and increased CVD (among other conditions). Alice seems competent except for math-related skills (MoCA math and Finances), but we don’t have evidence of cognitive decline - in fact this seems like normal since Henry took care of finances before he died. The MoCA score is close to the cut-off, but the MoCA is not used as a diagnostic tool and Alice otherwise seems fine. Orthostatic hypotension (headrush) is an age-related change.

stem: Which of the following activities would not be considered a Basic Activity of Daily Living?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Housework is an instrumental activity of daily living.

From 04 - Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment. Basic ADLs are the self-care tasks, DEATH: Dressing, Eating, Ambulating, Toileting/continence, Hygiene. Instrumental ADLs are the more cognitively demanding tasks of running a household, SHAFT: Shopping, Housework, Accounting, Food preparation, Telephone/transportation.

  • C - housework is the H of SHAFT, an IADL.
  • A, B, D - toileting, dressing and eating are all DEATH items.

The distinction matters clinically: because IADLs need more cognitive skill, they are the first to need help as cognition declines (the Clinical Frailty Scale's “mildly frail” step is defined by it).

stem: There are several types of dementia. Which of the following is a correct description?

options.html: Alzheimer’s dementia is characterized by amnesia, apraxia, agnosia, but normal physical exam findings.

Lewy-Body Dementia begins with the loss of memory, followed by executive and visuospatial functioning. Physical exam is normal.
Behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia is characterized by excessive crying at funerals and compulsive binge-eating
Language-variant frontotemporal dementia involves a dramatic increase in language proficiency at the expense of memory

answer:
The correct answer is A.

These are classic presentations of Alzheimer’s dementia. Vascular dementia involves strokes and damage to the brain which would increase leg reflex sensitivity. Lewy-Body dementia involves memory loss after executive and visuospatial function, as well as symptoms of Parkinsonism during physical exam. Frontotemporal dementia involves a normal MoCA test result, but behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia is characterized by a lack of empathy and laughing at a funeral.

Her lack of alertness and inability to recite months of the year backwards suggest delirium. Corticospinal tract: Primary Motor Cortex -> Internal Capsule -> Medulla -> Dorsal Horn in spinal cord
Spinothalamic tract: Primary Motor Cortex -> Internal Capsule -> Medulla -> Ventral Horn in spinal cord
Spinothalamic tract: Primary Motor Cortex -> Internal Capsule -> Medulla -> Dorsal Horn in spinal cord

The corticospinal tract begins in the primary cortex and traverses down the spinal tract. Efferent nerves leave the spinal tract through the ventral horns. The Spinothalamic tract begins in the spinal cord and ascends toward the brain.

stem: What of the following statements about the dorsal column tract and the spinothalamic tract are true? i) Dorsal columns transmit sensory information while the spinothalamic tract transmits motor information ii) The dorsal column tracts decussates (crosses over) at the medulla while the spinothalamic tract crosses over at the level of the spinal cord iii) The dorsal column tract and the spinothalamic tract both involve a synapse at the thalamus

The correct answer is B.

Both the spinothalamic system and dorsal column system transmit sensory information to the brain; the former transmits sensations of pain and temperature, and the latter transmits sensations of vibrations and proprioception. Both synapse at the thalamus, which relays sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex

stem: Which option is an accurate description of frailty or frail patients?

options.html: Frailty is a necessary and inevitable component of aging.
Frailty is the co-occurrence of multiple conditions, diseases, or illnesses.
Frailty is a syndrome associated with decreased resistance to stressors
Frail patients are more likely to be hospitalized but their hospital stays are relatively short
Patients who score CFS 9 on the frailty spectrum are completely dependent and approaching the end of life.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Frail patients have a diminished functional reserve and reduced capacity to maintain homeostasis in the presence of stressors. Frailty is not inevitable, but frail patients are more likely to be hospitalized and have longer stays in hospitals. Lastly, CFS 9 is associated with terminally-ill patients, who have less than six months of life. The description provided is in line with CFS 8.

stem: Beatrice, a 70 year old woman, shares that she has been experiencing seizures. With regards to medical fitness to drive, the next best step for the physician is:

options.html: Inform the patient to stop driving and inform the Ministry of Transportation
Seizures are considered a low-risk medical conditions so Taylor can continue driving for now
Explore with the patient how her seizures are impacting her ability to operate a vehicle
Explore with the patient other means of transportation asides from driving

answer:
The correct answer is C.

It’s important to explore how a condition affects one’s functional abilities before jumping to action.

A social worker supports both patients and caregivers by providing information on alternative living arrangements such as seniors apartments and retirement homes
A physiotherapist assesses a patient’s mobility and cognition in driving.
Registered dieticians assess an individual’s nutrition and risk for nutrition-related conditions. They offer education on different forms of supplementation

The correct answer is D.

The role of a physiotherapist is unrelated to cognition in driving. Physiotherapists provide education and tools to optimize a patient’s mobility.

stem: On the topic of elder abuse, which statement is true?

options.html: Elder abuse is more common if the abuser is financially dependent on the elder patient.
Elder abuse is less common if the patient is perceived as frail.
Elder abuse in long-term-care facilities may in part be due to the currently legislated minimum caregivers-to-residents ratio of 1-to-8.
When caring for elder patients, caregivers experience a high degree of stress, but this does not correlate to increased rates of elder abuse.
Rates of elder abuse have remained constant over the past ten years.

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Elder abuse increases as frailty increases. There is currently no legislation on the ratio of caregivers to patients in long-term-care facilities. Caregiver burnout is definitely correlated with elder abuse, and rates of elder abuse have increased in the past ten years in part due to lack of funding and changes in pharmacologic treatments of elderly patients.

Two women of the same age with the same condition, of the same socioeconomic status, receiving the same treatment

There are many individual differences from the genetic level to the environmental level, and identical outcomes in treatment are rare.

answer:

Some drugs don’t have a specific target, such as laxatives that irate the walls of our guts, or antacids which modify stomach pH.

stem: In the presence of Drug B, Drug A cannot reach the maximal response regardless of dose. Which of the following is true?

options.html: Drug B affects the efficacy and is a reversible competitive antagonist
Drug B has no effect on the EC50 and is a noncompetitive antagonist
Drug B affects the potency and is a reversible competitive antagonist
Drug B binds to the orthosteric site and is a noncompetitive antagonist

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Drug B does not affect the EC50 (or potency), but does affect the maximum dose response (it has an effect on efficacy). This indicates a noncompetitive antagonist.

stem: Which definition below, pertaining to pharmacodynamics, is incorrect?

options.html: A partial agonist binds to a receptor and results in an increased activity relative to the baseline.
An inverse agonist binds to a receptor, resulting in a decreased activity relative to the baseline.
An allosteric antagonist binds to the same binding site as the receptor agonist and decreases the activity of an agonist.
Competitive antagonists increase the required concentration for an agonist to elicit its maximal effect.
Noncompetitive antagonists affect the potency of an agonist but leave the efficacy unchanged.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Allosteric inactivators bind to a location on the receptor that is different than the binding site.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Consider the dose response curve below for three different drugs. Which of the following statements is false?

options.html: Drug A is more potent than Drug B and C
Drug C can be Drug B in the presence of a competitive antagonist
Drug C can be a partial agonist
Drug A can be Drug B combined with a non-competitive antagonist

If Drug C is a partial agonist, we would see a reduction in the maximum response (reduced efficacy).

stem: Heroin is a mu-opioid receptor agonist. A pharmacologist is studying the effect of a novel drug, BK-562, on heroin’s dose-response, and early studies have shown that BK- 562 reduces the potency of heroin. It was also noted by the pharmacologist that if the concentration of heroin is sufficiently large, there is no change in maximal effectiveness. Which of the following statements is false?

options.html: BK-562 could be a partial agonist for the mu-opioid receptor.
BK-562 could not be a noncompetitive antagonist for the mu-opioid receptor.
BK-562 could decrease the EC50 of heroin.
BK-562 could be a competitive antagonist for the mu-opioid receptor.
BK-562 could be an inverse agonist for the mu-opioid receptor.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Reducing the potency of a drug has the effect of increasing its ED50 of a drug.

stem: The first-pass metabolism effect refers to the phenomena that:

options.html: Parenteral (IM, SC, IV) drugs are sometimes metabolized in extracellular spaces reducing the bioavailability
Oral drugs are sometimes metabolized in the liver reducing the bioavailability
Oral and Transdermal drugs are sometimes able to attain sustained release due to slowed metabolic degradation
Most drugs are able to bypass metabolic degradation on their first pass in the body

answer:
The correct answer is B.

First-pass metabolism is when certain oral drugs are metabolized in the liver or digestive tract before absorption into the bloodstream, reducing the bioavailability (concentration of drug in circulation). Note, parenteral drugs may still be metabolized before achieving main circulation, but first-pass metabolism refers to the metabolism which occurs during oral administration.

stem: Which of the following statements is correct with regards to Drug Distribution?

options.html: Hydrophilic molecules are more easily able to cross the blood brain barrier
Drugs that have a high affinity to plasma proteins (e.g albumin) tend to distribute faster
Lipid-rich areas of low vasculature like the fat and bone can act as a reservoir for the drug
Areas of low metabolism like the kidney and liver receive the drug faster

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Lipophilic molecules are more easily able to pass the BBB. Drugs with low affinity to plasma proteins distribute faster, areas of high blood flow receive the drug faster.

stem: What major purpose do Cytochrome P450 macromolecules play in pharmacokinetics?

options.html: These enzymes mediate most oxidation/reduction reactions in phase 1 metabolism
These transporters are key transporters in the absorption of drugs in the intestine
These enzymes facilitate reactions that make the drugs more lipophilic and increase drug solubility
These enzymes often participate in conjugation reactions in phase 2 metabolism

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Many Phase 1 metabolism reactions are performed by CYP450 enzymes, which reduce the lipophilicity and increase the hydrophilicity.

stem:
A patient’s intestinal bacteria is severely diminished. With regards to drug pharmacokinetics which process would be significantly affected?

  1. Drug Metabolism
  2. Enterohepatic recycling
  3. Biliary excretion
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Intestinal bacteria play a large role in drug metabolism and process drug conjugates in enterohepatic recycling to reintroduce them into circulation.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which statement on the topic of pharmacokinetics is true? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

options.html: The first-pass metabolism refers to initial metabolism of a drug by the digestive system before entering systemic circulation
All drugs administered intravenously will have a higher bioavailability than drugs administered orally
Elevated blood concentrations of albumin will increase the delivery of lipophilic drugs to their target tissue
Drugs entering the brain must be hydrophobic to pass the blood-brain-barrier.
The most common routes of elimination are renal excretion and biliary excretion.

answer:
The correct answer is A, B, E.

Albumin allows for the transfer of lipophilic molecules in the bloodstream. Elevated albumin would sequester these lipophilic molecules and reduce delivery to target organs. While lipophilic drugs more easily pass through the blood-brain-barrier, drugs can also pass through the blood-brain-barrier via membrane transport proteins

An advantage of transdermal application is the prolonged release of medication.
An advantage of sublingual application is its delayed absorption.
An advantage of subcutaneous application is its prolonged effect.
An advantage of intramuscular application is its suitability for oil-based drugs.

The main advantage of sublingual application is its immediate (not delayed) absorption.

stem: A physician wants to establish a minimum plasma level of 4 mg/L of Drug A but wants to ensure that plasma concentration does not surpass the toxic level of 8 mg/L. Drug A has a half-life of one day. Assuming a bioavailability of 1 (100%), which of the following routines would best achieve this given your knowledge of steady state concentration. What is the best prescription option available?

options.html: Prescribe a 500 mg tablet to be taken once daily (produces a plasma concentration of 8 mg/L)
Prescribe a 250 mg tablet to be taken once daily (produces a plasma concentration of 4 mg/L)
Prescribe a 500 mg tablet to be taken once every 2 days
Prescribe a 125 mg tablet to be taken once daily (produces a plasma concentration of 2 mg/L

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Prescribing a dose that leads to 4 mg/L will eventually lead to a minimum plasma concentration of 4 mg/L at which point taking another dose will not surpass the 8mg/L threshold.

stem: A half-life of a drug is estimated to be about 2 days in the human body. It also has a very large range between ED50 and TD50. Which statement below is true?

options.html: It would take about 3-5 days for the drug to reach state-state concentration if the drug is administered every day.
The steady-state concentration will not be changed if the dosing interval is doubled but the daily amount of drug administered is the same.
The therapeutic window changes if the dose is increased.
The maintenance dose often precedes the loading dose to establish a high plasma concentration quickly.
A patient treated with this drug would likely require rigorous analysis to avoid toxicity issues.

answer:
The correct answer is B.

As long as the total daily dose is the same, adjusting the frequency of doses will not affect the steady-state concentration of the drug. For this drug, steady-state would be achieved after 6-10 days (3-5 times the half-life). Since the therapeutic window is so large (i.e., large difference between ED50 and TD50), the patient would likely not need rigorous analysis for toxicity issues.

The patient occasionally forgets to take his daily dose of a drug with a large therapeutic window.
The patient occasionally doubles their daily dose of a drug with a small therapeutic window.
The patient occasionally doubles their daily dose of a drug with a large therapeutic window.

The correct answer is C.

The small therapeutic window means that too large of a dose may lead to toxicity issues.

options.html: Safety – will my patient be harmed taking this medication?
Tolerability – Will the patient suffer side effects taking this medication?
Effectiveness – Is there evidence that this medication will help the patient?
Pharmacology – will the patient suffer any adverse drug reactions with this medicine?
Simplicity – is the dosage regimen as simple as possible to increase adherence?

The correct answer is D.

The P in the STEPS acronym stands for Price - will the patient’s insurance or benefits be able to pay for this medication? If not, will they be able to afford this medication?

Women are more prone to adverse drug events than men
Increased body fat composition tends to decrease volume of distribution in medications

options.html: A diet rich in grapefruit activates CYP3A4, increasing metabolism of some drugs.
The health of the liver affects the metabolism of drugs.
The health of the kidney affects the elimination of drugs and metabolites.
Polymorphisms in the CYP2C9 genes change enzyme activity.
Copy number variation of CYP450 enzymes affects drug metabolism.

Grapefruit inhibits CYP3A4 in the small intestine, which decreases the metabolism of some drugs and increases their bioavailability.

answer:

stem: Which of the following is the fastest response to a drop in blood pressure:
answer:
The correct answer is C.

From 02 - Introduction to Blood Pressure Regulation. The lecture splits blood pressure control in two: the autonomic nervous system is the short-term, rapid response, and hormonal mechanisms are the long-term, slow one. A fall in pressure unloads the high-pressure baroreceptors in the aortic arch and carotid sinus, and the brain responds by raising heart rate and sympathetic tone to the arterioles - raising CO and TPR, and so MAP (MAP = CO x TPR).

  • A, D - the RAAS and aldosterone are hormonal: renin must generate angiotensin II, and aldosterone works by changing Na+ reabsorption and volume - the slow arm.
  • B - a fall in GFR is a consequence of reduced renal perfusion, and any renal volume-conserving effect is slow, not a reflex.

stem: Which of the following is true about the interaction of the cardiovascular system with the respiratory system?

options.html: Oxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle to the lungs for gas exchange
Deoxygenated blood from the systemic circulation will undergo gas exchange at the lungs before returning to the heart.
Oxygen is removed from the blood and carbon dioxide is added to the blood during gas exchange
Unlike most arteries, the pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood to the lungs

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Deoxygenated blood from the systemic circulation is returned to the right side of the heart through the superior and inferior vena cava. This blood is transported to the lungs via the pulmonary arteries. At the lungs, gas exchange occurs: oxygen is added to the blood and carbon dioxide removed. Then the pulmonary veins will transport the oxygenated blood to the left side of the heart, which will pump the blood into the systemic circulation. Note that the pulmonary arteries and veins are sort of unique. Most veins in the systemic circulation carry deoxygenated blood and most arteries carry oxygenated blood – this is not the case for the pulmonary arteries and veins.

stem: Rank each pathology report term from least (1) to most (5) malignant.
answer:
The pairings:

TerminologyRank (1 least to 5 most malignant)
Atypia Present, Cannot exclude malignancy3
Suspicion for Malignancy4
Atypia Present, Favour Reactive2
Positive for malignancy5 - most malignant
Negative for malignancy1 - least malignant

From 06 - Communication of the Pathology Report. When a diagnosis is not clear-cut the pathologist writes a narrative report using a graded vocabulary of malignancy risk. The lecture's scale runs positive → suspicious → atypia (cannot exclude malignancy) → atypia (favour reactive) → negative; reversed for least-to-most:

  • 1 - negative for malignancy.
  • 2 - atypia present, favour reactive: abnormal cells, but the pathologist leans benign.
  • 3 - atypia present, cannot exclude malignancy: abnormal cells with malignancy left open.
  • 4 - suspicious for malignancy: probably cancer, short of certainty.
  • 5 - positive for malignancy.

The two atypia terms are the trap: favour reactive leans benign, cannot exclude does not.

stem: Lindsay is a 31-year-old female patient who is administered isoproterenol to treat her bradycardia by increasing her heart rate. The potency and efficacy of isoproterenol will be unchanged

If a CYP enzyme that metabolizes Prodrug X is inhibited, then the plasma levels of Drug X will be lower than expected

answer:
The correct answer is B.

There is significant genetic variation among CYP genes. Polymorphisms in CYP genes largely explain the individual variability seen in response to medications. A particular drug may be toxic in poor metabolizers, while ultra-rapid metabolizers may have no response to the same dose of the same drug.

stem: Which of the following is false regarding excretion?

Once biliary-excreted drugs have entered the intestines they are destined to be excreted in the feces

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Drugs excreted in the bile enter the intestines where they have 1 of 2 fates. The drug can be excreted in the feces. It may also be processed by intestinal bacteria (usually resulting in the drug being deconjugated) and the resulting free drug can re-enter the systemic circulation. The latter process is termed enterohepatic recycling and is important for certain drugs to maintain its proper therapeutic concentration. An example of a drug that uses this mechanism is oral contraception.

stem: A 55 y/o F patient presents to ER with right lower quadrant sharp abdominal pain, you measure her blood pressure to be 160/93. What is her mean arterial pressure?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

MAP=DP+1/3(SP-DP)

From 02 - Introduction to Blood Pressure Regulation. The lecture's formula is MAP = DP + 1/3 (SP - DP). Here the pulse pressure is 160 - 93 = 67; a third of it is 22.3; and 93 + 22.3 = 115.3 mmHg.

  • A (114.7), B (121.4), D (109.3) - none follows from the formula.

The check worth remembering: MAP is weighted toward diastolic pressure, so it always sits below the simple average of systolic and diastolic (here 126.5). The abdominal pain in the stem is a distractor; the question is pure arithmetic.

stem: Around 1am, worried new parents of a 2 month old baby have reached out to you regarding their child feeling unwell. You recall that the baby has a rare genetic condition that results in an overexpression of ion leaky channels and may induce significant solute loss from their ECF. What are you worried about in regards to their ICF/ECF volumes as well as the respective osmolarity?

options.html: ICF volume decrease, ECF volume increase, Osmolarity reduce in both.
ICF and ECF volume both decrease, Osmolarity reduce in only ICF.
ICF volume increase, ECF volume decrease, Osmolarity reduce in only ICF.
ICF and ECF volume both increase, Osmolarity reduce in both.
ICF volume increase, ECF volume decrease, Osmolarity reduce in both.

answer:
The correct answer is E.

From 01 - An Introduction to Body Fluids Regulation. The lecture's dehydration logic runs in reverse here. Losing solute from the ECF makes the ECF hypo-osmotic, so water follows its gradient into the cells: ICF volume rises, ECF volume falls. Water keeps moving until the two compartments are iso-osmotic again, so osmolarity ends up lower in both - the cells cannot hold a different osmolarity from their surroundings.

  • A, D - ECF volume cannot rise when water is leaving it for the cells.
  • B - both volumes cannot fall with no net fluid loss; water shifts, it does not vanish.
  • C - right volumes, but osmolarity equilibrates, so it cannot fall in the ICF alone.

stem: After cell death, the majority of tissues can heal by _____.
answer:
The correct answer is D.

The majority of tissue could do regeneration repair.

From 05 - Cellular Stress & Repair. After injury, tissue either regenerates (normal function restored) or is repaired by scar. Regeneration happens in tissues made of labile and stable cells when the injury is not too severe - which covers most tissues (skin and GI epithelium constantly, hepatocytes from G0). Only permanent cells (cardiac myocytes, neurons, skeletal muscle) always heal by scarring.

  • A - fibrous scarring is the fallback for permanent cells, severe injury or damaged supporting structures, not the majority.
  • B, C - hyperplasia and hypertrophy are adaptations to stress (more cells, bigger cells), not the healing outcome after cell death.

stem: A 37-year-old woman comes into clinic with a right breast lump that she is worried about because her mother died of breast cancer. What are the next 3 most reasonable steps as a physician? (Choose 3 options)

options.html: Obtain complete history and physical exam
Request thoracic MRI to stage the cancer
Order CT of head to rule out brain metastasis
Ultrasound with possible fine needle biopsy
Order full body PET scan to rule out distant metastasis

answer:
The correct answer is A, D, F.

A – Always do history and physical first unless the patient is unstable. B- MRI is almost never a good first line test. C- This is assuming it’s a cancer which it is likely not. D- Obtaining additional information is quick and may provide valuable insight about hormone levels etc. E- While this may be the best diagnostic test, we have no firm reason to suspect cancer yet. F- This is less invasive and more appropriate to first rule out common things like cysts etc. G-PET is only to stage proven or highly suspected cancers.

stem: A 50-year-old woman presents with a breast lump that has been present for several months. She also complains of night sweats which she thinks is related to her recent onset of menopause. On physical examination, you detect a firm, non-tender mass in the upper outer region of the breast. Mammogram shows a mass with irregular borders that measures approximately 3cm in size. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.html: Perform a stereotactic-guided aspiration, send for pathology
Use a large bore (21G) needle to obtain a core biopsy, send for pathology
Reassure patient that new lumps are normal in menopausal women due to fluctuating hormonal levels
Refer to surgery and oncology immediately for excision and chemotherapy

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Red flags for breast mass are present in this case (firm, non-tender, irregular borders, older age). Night sweats can be associated with menopause, but is also a B-symptom which is characteristic of malignant neoplasm. Thus, aspiration (cyst, abscess) and reassurance are inappropriate, and needle core biopsy (staging) needs to be obtained prior to surgical excision/chemotherapy initiation.

stem: A 65-year-old woman presents with a painless lump in her breast that has been slowly increasing in size over the past few months. Biopsy demonstrates atypical cells with increased mitotic rate. Which of the following terms best describes this type of cell proliferation?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

From 02 - Approach to Neoplasia. A neoplasm is an abnormal mass arising from excessive cell division and evasion of apoptosis. A slowly enlarging lump whose biopsy shows atypical cells with a raised mitotic rate is that - abnormal cells proliferating autonomously.

  • A - hypertrophy is larger cells with no new cells (05 - Cellular Stress & Repair).
  • B - hyperplasia is more cells, but normal ones driven by hormones or growth factors, not atypical ones.
  • C - metaplasia replaces one differentiated cell type with another; it adds no mass of atypical cells.

stem: Mrs. E is a 71 year old woman seeing you in your family clinic. She complains that recently she has noticed that she can’t hear high pitched noises, she finds it harder to read street signs at night, wakes up to pee most nights, and finds that she is constipated more often than she is used to. Which of her symptoms are normal changes due to aging?

options.html: High frequency hearing loss and night-vision loss only
High frequency hearing loss and nocturia only.
More frequent nocturia and constipation only.
Night vision loss and more frequent nocturia only.
All of her symptoms are normal changes due to ageing.

answer:
The correct answer is E.

Normal age-related changes must meet 5 criteria: cumulative over time, progressive in nature, universal, intrinsic, and deleterious. Common changes include: higher risk of orthostatic hypotension, decreased thermoregulation, higher risk of dehydration, nocturia, wrinkles and grey hair, easier to lose ambulation, vision loss (especially night vision), high frequency hearing loss, cardiac diastolic dysfunction, finding food less appealing, constipation, decreased inflammatory response, endocrine changes, and incomplete bladder emptying.

stem: Identify each activity as either an Activity of Daily Living (ADL) or an Instrumental Activity of Daily Living (IADL).
answer:
The pairings:

ActivityADL or IADL
AmbulatingADL (activity of daily living)
CookingIADL (instrumental activity of daily living)
DressingADL (activity of daily living)
EatingADL (activity of daily living)
FinancesIADL (instrumental activity of daily living)
Hygiene (bathing)ADL (activity of daily living)
Medication managementIADL (instrumental activity of daily living)
ShoppingIADL (instrumental activity of daily living)
Social engagementIADL (instrumental activity of daily living)
TelephoneIADL (instrumental activity of daily living)
ToiletingADL (activity of daily living)
TransportationIADL (instrumental activity of daily living)
TransferringADL (activity of daily living)

From 04 - Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment.

  • Ambulating is the A of DEATH, a basic ADL: moving from one position to another (transfers) and walking independently. It is physical self-care, not a household task that needs planning.
  • Cooking is the F of SHAFT (Food preparation), an IADL: it needs planning, sequencing and safety judgment, not just the physical ability to feed oneself. Do not confuse it with eating, which is a basic ADL.
  • Dressing is the D of DEATH, a basic ADL: selecting appropriate clothing and putting it on.
  • Eating is the E of DEATH, a basic ADL: the ability to feed oneself. Preparing the food is a different task - cooking is an IADL.
  • Finances are the A of SHAFT (Accounting), an IADL: the ability to pay bills and manage money, a cognitively demanding task of running a household rather than self-care.
  • Hygiene is the H of DEATH, a basic ADL: bathing and grooming oneself and keeping up dental, nail and hair care.
  • Managing medications is the extra M the SHAFT note adds to the IADLs: obtaining medications and taking them as prescribed. It depends on memory and organization rather than physical self-care.
  • Shopping is the S of SHAFT, an IADL: acquiring food and clothing.
  • Social engagement is not one of the named SHAFT items, but it belongs on the IADL side by the same logic: it is a higher-order activity of living in the community, not basic self-care of the body - and none of the DEATH items (Dressing, Eating, Ambulating, Toileting, Hygiene) covers it.
  • Using the telephone is a T of SHAFT, an IADL, along with mail, internet and email.
  • Toileting is the T of DEATH, a basic ADL: getting to and from the toilet, using it appropriately and cleaning oneself, plus continence - control of bladder and bowel.
  • Transportation is a T of SHAFT, an IADL: driving or using public transport.

The split to remember: ADLs = DEATH (Dressing, Eating, Ambulating, Toileting, Hygiene), the basic self-care tasks; IADLs = SHAFT (Shopping, Housework, Accounting, Food preparation, Telephone/Transportation) plus managing medications, the household tasks that need more cognitive skill.

Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) can be remembered by the mnemonic DEAT(T)H: Dressing, Eating, Ambulating, Toileting, Transferring, Hygiene (Bathing). Instrumental ADLs are shopping, transportation, cooking, finances, telephone, medications, social engagement.

The Canadian healthcare system is actually a group of pseudo-independently run provincial systems with different rules. Drugs are the largest expense and are forecasted to become an even larger part of the pie with increasingly sophisticated drug developments.

stem: Consider a patient receiving chemotherapy for a significantly large solid tumour. Which of the following factors would lead to better drug distribution?

options.html: The tumour is in the CNS

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Factors that are associated with better drug distribution include high lipid solubility and increased blood flow to target tissues. It’s difficult for drugs to reach tumours in the CNS due to the blood brain barrier. Blood pressure is not a major factor affecting drug distribution. Intravenous drug distribution would result in increased bioavailability but would not affect drug distribution.

stem: Which of the following would be considered an unpredictable adverse drug reaction?

options.html: A patient experiences hives and wheezing after taking ibuprofen for the first time
A patient experiences hair loss as a side effect of chemotherapy for a breast tumour
A patient who has been taking amiodarone, an anti-arrhythmic drug, begins drinking grapefruit juice with their breakfast daily and finds that their arrhythmias have become more frequent.
A patient takes their prescription sedative medication while having alcoholic drinks with friends. He later stops breathing and becomes unresponsive

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Option a) describes an allergic reaction which is classified as an unpredictable ADR. Options b), c), and d) describe a side effect, a drug-food interaction, and a drug-drug interaction, respectively, all of which are classified as predictable ADRs because these effects can be predicted from the pharmacologic actions of the drug.

answer:
The correct answer is A, B, C, E, I.

stem: Which of the following practices correctly follows the principles of geriatric prescribing?

options.html: Always err on the side of undertreating rather than overtreating older patients
Consider discontinuing or dose-reducing existing medications rather than treating an ADE with another medication
Start medications at a higher dose to compensate for decreased metabolism in the elderly and then make adjustments based on response
Non-compliance is rare in older populations and when it occurs it’s usually unintentional, so there’s no need to worry about it.

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Reducing polypharmacy has benefits in patient safety and adherence, but it’s important not to undertreat older patients especially for common issues such as pain, hypertension, and stroke prevention (a is false). The principle of “Think drugs” tries to avoid prescribing cascades where an ADE is incorrectly attributed to a new medical problem, leading to the inappropriate use of a second drug (b is true). The principle of “Start low go slow” recommends prescribing one medication at a time at a low dose and increasing gradually (c is false). The principle of “assessing adherence” recognizes that 25-50% of older patients are noncompliant and about 75% of non-compliance is intentional (to cut costs or avoid side effects etc.) (d is false).

stem: During the summer between your first and second year of med school, you get SROP funding to analyze data for a drug trial at LHSC’s cancer center. In this phase of the drug trial, Drug X is being evaluated for safety in a small number of healthy patients. What phase of drug development and approval is this drug at?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Clinical Phase I is conducted to assess the safety profile of the drug. Clinical Phase II is conducted to assess the efficacy of the drug. Clinical Phase III also assess efficacy in a larger population. Clinical Phase IV is post-marketing surveillance of a drug’s long-term effects.

stem: A drug that permanently binds to a receptor in a non-competitive manner would impact which of the following metrics?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

stem: Match each prescription abbreviation to its meaning.
answer:
The pairings:

AbbreviationMeaning
POOrally
BIDTwice a day
PRNAs needed
ACBefore meal
ODRight eye

From 05 - Principles of Clinical Pharmacology (its prescription abbreviations table).

  • PO - orally.
  • BID - twice a day; the frequency series is q.d., b.i.d., t.i.d., q.i.d. for once to four times a day.
  • PRN - as needed; 01 - Approach To Prescribing adds that a PRN order still needs a maximum frequency.
  • AC - before meals; p.c. is after meals.
  • OD - right eye, paired with O.S. (left eye) and O.U. (both eyes).

OD is the trap: it reads like “once daily”, but the lecture's once-daily abbreviation is q.d.
